# IntelReap

> IntelReap runs free live checks of your network and device (public IP, network route, VPN and proxy status, WebRTC exposure, latency, browser and GPU data) and publishes plain-language guides that explain the results. No account is needed.

## Live tools
- [Capability Matrix](https://intelreap.com/intelligence/capability): Live browser capability detection across 56 features — AI, storage, graphics, and connectivity support explained.
- [Device Intelligence Panel](https://intelreap.com/intelligence/device): Live OS, browser, CPU, RAM, screen, and sensor data — your complete device profile explained parameter by parameter.
- [Fingerprint and Leak Detection Panel Explained](https://intelreap.com/intelligence/fingerprinting): A deep dive into browser fingerprinting and leak detection — audio, canvas, font and ClientRects fingerprinting, bot detection, ad blocker detection, DNS-adjacent leak signals, and GPS-vs-IP geolocation comparison, explained parameter by parameter.
- [Graphics Engine Panel](https://intelreap.com/intelligence/graphics): Live GPU, WebGL, WebGPU, and graphics tier analysis — your rendering capability explained parameter by parameter.
- [Live Intelligence Feed — What Just Happened?](https://intelreap.com/intelligence/live-feed): Real-time event log of every engine action, network change, API call, security flag, and AI summary — your live scan feed explained parameter by parameter.
- [Live Network Monitor Explained](https://intelreap.com/intelligence/live-network): Real-time latency, bandwidth, stability index, packet loss estimate, jitter, and connection quality — your live network performance explained parameter by parameter.
- [Network Identity Panel Explained](https://intelreap.com/intelligence/network-identity): Live IP address lookup, ISP, geolocation, timezone, connection type, and mobile/proxy/hosting flags — your full network identity explained parameter by parameter.
- [ASN and Network Route Intelligence Explained](https://intelreap.com/intelligence/network-route): Live ASN lookup, network tier classification, BGP route status, allocation registry, and peering data — see exactly what network infrastructure you're connecting through, explained parameter by parameter.
- [Performance Intelligence Panel Explained](https://intelreap.com/intelligence/performance): Live page load time, TTFB, DNS lookup, TCP connection, TLS handshake, DOM processing, memory usage, and resource stats — your browser performance explained parameter by parameter.
- [Browser and Rendering Speed Panel Explained](https://intelreap.com/intelligence/rendering-speed): Live Core Web Vitals — LCP, FCP, CLS, INP, TTFB — plus JS execution, DOM manipulation, canvas render, and memory benchmark scores, explained parameter by parameter.
- [Global Intelligence Scoreboard Explained](https://intelreap.com/intelligence/scoreboard): Your global intelligence score across nine weighted dimensions — network, identity, privacy, device, graphics, security, capability, performance, and speed — explained parameter by parameter.
- [Security & Privacy Panel](https://intelreap.com/intelligence/security): Live security posture — HTTPS, WebRTC exposure, permissions, and your security score explained parameter by parameter.
- [VPN, Proxy and Routing Panel Explained](https://intelreap.com/intelligence/vpn-proxy): Live VPN detection, proxy detection, TOR exit node check, datacenter routing, trust score, fraud score, and route classification — your routing exposure explained parameter by parameter.

## Guides and explainers
- [Two Internet Providers in One House: Is It Possible?](https://intelreap.com/learn/can-you-have-two-isps-in-one-house): Yes — you can legally have two internet providers in one house. Learn how dual-WAN works, which routers support it, load balancing vs failover, costs, and how to check ISP availability in your area.
- [Does a VPN Change or Hide Your MAC Address?](https://intelreap.com/learn/does-a-vpn-change-your-mac-address): No — a VPN does not change your MAC address. Learn what a VPN actually changes, whether ExitLag is a VPN, how to use VPN in incognito, bind qBittorrent to a VPN, and more.
- [How to Find a Printer's IP Address on Any Device](https://intelreap.com/learn/find-printer-ip-address): Find your printer's IP address in under a minute: printer menu, Windows, Mac, Linux or your router. Includes a device step picker and diagrams.
- [How to Find Your Router's IP Address on Any Device](https://intelreap.com/learn/find-router-ip-address): Find your router's IP address (default gateway) on Windows, Mac, Linux, iPhone or Android. Includes a device step picker, default address list and diagrams.
- [How to Fix Slow DNS Lookup (Test It, Then Fix It)](https://intelreap.com/learn/how-to-fix-slow-dns-lookup): Slow DNS lookup delays every page. Time your resolver, compare public ones live, then change DNS, flush the cache and check your VPN and router.
- [How to Protect Your Privacy Online](https://intelreap.com/learn/how-to-protect-your-privacy-online): Practical steps to protect your privacy online in 2026 — VPNs, browser fingerprinting, password security, DNS privacy, mobile tracking, and the tools that actually make a difference.
- [WebRTC Leak Test and How to Shield Your IP](https://intelreap.com/learn/webrtc-leak-test-and-shield): WebRTC can expose your real IP address even behind a VPN. Test for leaks instantly and learn how to disable or shield WebRTC in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Brave, and Edge.
- [What Is a GPU? Explained Simply](https://intelreap.com/learn/what-is-a-gpu): A GPU is a processor built for massively parallel computation. Learn what GPU stands for, how it works, how it differs from a CPU, integrated vs dedicated GPU, VRAM, and how to check what GPU you have.
- [What Is a VPN Concentrator?](https://intelreap.com/learn/what-is-a-vpn-concentrator): A VPN concentrator is a dedicated network device that handles hundreds or thousands of simultaneous VPN tunnels. Learn how it works, how it differs from a VPN router and gateway, and when to use one.
- [What Is an IP Address? Types and How It Works](https://intelreap.com/learn/what-is-an-ip-address): An IP address is the number that identifies a device on a network. Learn IPv4 vs IPv6, public vs private, NAT and DHCP, and check your own IP live.
- [What Is Device Fingerprinting? How to Block It](https://intelreap.com/learn/what-is-device-fingerprinting): Device fingerprinting identifies you without cookies by combining browser, hardware, and network signals. Learn how it works, who uses it, and how to reduce your fingerprint exposure.
- [What Is Reverse IP Lookup?](https://intelreap.com/learn/what-is-reverse-ip-lookup): Reverse IP lookup finds every domain hosted on a given IP address. Learn how it works, why sites share IPs, what it's used for, and its limitations for security research and competitor analysis.
- [What Is VPN Passthrough? PPTP and IPsec Explained](https://intelreap.com/learn/what-is-vpn-passthrough): VPN passthrough lets VPN client traffic travel through a NAT router to an external VPN server. Learn what it is, when you need it, and how to enable it — plus why most modern VPNs don't require it at all.
- [Why Does My Internet Speed Fluctuate?](https://intelreap.com/learn/why-does-my-internet-speed-fluctuate): Internet speed fluctuates due to congestion, modem age, router limits, Wi-Fi interference, or ISP throttling. Diagnose the exact cause and fix it with this complete 2026 guide.
- [GPU Troubleshooting: Common Questions Answered](https://intelreap.com/guides/gpu-troubleshooting-guide): Why is my GPU usage so high? How to reset a GPU, what Ti means, undervolting explained, hardware accelerated GPU scheduling, and whether to remove GPU when moving PC — complete 2026 guide.
- [How to Enable WebGL in Chrome, Firefox and Safari](https://intelreap.com/guides/how-to-enable-webgl): WebGL not working in Chrome or Firefox? Step-by-step fixes for hardware acceleration, GPU blocklist issues, and 'a WebGL context could not be created' — plus how to enable WebGL in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge.
- [How to Find an IP Address on Any Device or Site](https://intelreap.com/guides/how-to-find-ip-address-of-any-device): Find your public IP with a live check, your device's IP on Windows, Mac, Linux, iPhone and Android, your router, another device on your network, or the IP address of a website or game server.
